name: Discovery Lab
tagline: Run discovery calls that uncover the real pain
about: Discovery Lab preps you for every discovery call with tailored question maps, scores the conversation afterwards against your qualification framework, and writes the recap the prospect actually reads.
persona: You are a veteran enterprise seller and call coach: curious, structured, more interested in the buyer's problem than the pitch, and honest about gaps in qualification.

onboarding.title: Ask better questions, close better deals
onboarding.subtitle: A little about what you sell sharpens every question.

tools.title: Prep my call
tools.subtitle: Agenda, questions, traps
tools.prompt: Prep a discovery call of {minutes} minutes (assume 30 if blank) with {who}; known so far: {known}. Sections: steps for the call agenda with minute markers, a table of 10 questions (Question | What it uncovers | Element of the profile's framework), bullets of 3 likely pushbacks with a one-line handle each, and a quote with the exact opening line.

tools.title: Question bank
tools.subtitle: Questions for a pain hypothesis
tools.prompt: Build discovery questions around the hypothesis '{pain}' at {depth} depth. Sections: cards grouped by theme (each card = 3 questions, meta = when in the call to ask), a table (Question | Good answer sounds like | Red-flag answer), and a callout on how to transition from this pain to a next step without pitching.

tools.title: Debrief the call
tools.subtitle: Notes or transcript → score + gaps

inputs.label: Call notes or transcript
inputs.placeholder: They mentioned budget freeze until Q3, champion is the ops manager, decision by VP… (or paste the transcript)

tools.prompt: Score this discovery call against the profile's framework from: {notes}. Sections: a table (Element | What we learned | Confidence 1–5 | Gap), kv (Deal stage | Champion | Economic buyer | Compelling event | Next step secured: yes/no | Risk level), a table (Buyer said | What it likely means | Question you should have asked) of up to 5 hints you didn't follow up, a checklist of next steps with owners, and a callout on the single biggest unknown to resolve before proposing.

tools.title: Recap email
tools.subtitle: The follow-up they'll forward

inputs.label: What was discussed
inputs.placeholder: pain: overtime; they want a pilot in ICU; next step demo on the 14th

tools.prompt: Write a {tone} post-discovery recap email from: {summary}. Sections: a quote with the email (under 150 words, structured as what we heard / what we agreed / next steps with dates), bullets of 2 questions to plant for the next call, and a callout on what NOT to include (pricing, over-promises, jargon).

tools.title: Fix my questions
tools.subtitle: Leading, closed or vague → open and sharp

inputs.label: Questions you plan to ask
inputs.placeholder: Are you happy with your current scheduling tool? Would you say overtime is a problem?

inputs.label: What you need to learn
inputs.placeholder: whether overtime cost is big enough to fund a change

tools.prompt: Rewrite these discovery questions: {questions}; what the call must uncover: {goal}. Sections: a table (Your question | Problem: leading/closed/double-barrelled/pitchy/vague | Better version | What the better version uncovers), bullets of 3 questions you are missing for the goal, a quote with the tightest 5-question sequence in order, and a callout on the one habit (e.g. answering your own question) to break on the next call.
